purpose: Count a start's store calls made after its guest ran as part of the time to running.
Acknowledge a discard without changing bytes.
Write one byte beyond the requested offset.
Accept a write exceeding the configured payload budget.
Lose the captured VMM state while retaining volume data.
Accept a handoff layout with the wrong volume size.
Accept a started VMM that omits a handed-off memory region.
Replace a successfully served source page with zeros.

Return zeros instead of volume bytes when the source answers that it no longer serves the VM. Its test is a destination whose source is released before its first read, over a checkpoint that holds every byte the guest wrote, so zeros differ from what the volume holds.
Leave the source sealed or paused after an abandoned migration. One test finds the guest paused, the other the release's failure missing from the error. Each fails alone.

Give a handoff up after its first failed receive while the source still holds its pages. One scenario's destination cannot reach the store for ten seconds, so only a retry hands the guest over; the other's refuses until the hold is over, which the handoff must outlast. Each fails alone.

Keep waiting on a listed source nothing can reach after its hold is over, a migration's source or a fork's parent's host. Only a source cut off while still listed leaves the hold as the one evidence, and no campaign draws that fault, so the two scenarios are its entry. Each fails alone.

Send a handoff's next receive while a host still reports an earlier one in flight. Only a receive whose caller hung up is in flight when a retry looks, and no campaign draws that fault, so the scenario is its entry.

Report every page of a handoff's set as the source's for the peer backing's whole life, which told a fork's child that pages it had published had no object. Only a destination checkpointed while its source still serves retires one of them, which is why this is that scenario's entry.

Report a page of a handoff's set as the source's while the volume names a checkpoint from before the handoff, which a hole always seems to be, so a page of zeros the destination published and retired is loaded as the source's own.

Ask the source for every page a destination loads, including one it published since the handoff, which answers with the version the guest wrote past. Only a destination whose arena gives back a page it published while its source still serves loads one.
Fault a destination's stream pages all at once, so the scheduler orders their slots, evictions and requests.
Forget that evicted private bytes exist in scratch storage. Its test spills a page the guest stored into, twice, and faults it back each time.
Leave a pager's spill file sparse instead of allocating its whole extent. Another writer then fills the filesystem, and the guest's next spill fails for want of space.
Give back a cold copy the guest stored into, as though it still held its origin's bytes.
Read a fault's whole read-ahead run before its page is installed, as the pager did before 2026-10-04. Every hop of a dependent chain of faults then waits for a run instead of a page.
Start the prefetch of the rest of a fault's run, then read the faulting page only once that prefetch is in. A fault beside a held prefetch then waits for it.
Read a page a prefetch is already reading again rather than wait for that read. A guest reading forwards then reads pages twice and no longer in runs.
Read the store for a fetch whose last caller left, after its read of the disk failed for that, though the disk holds the page a pull put there.
Map a page a capture write-protected writable again on the guest's store without making it unjournaled, so the next flush leaves out what the guest stored.
Forget at a seal the pages no journal entry holds yet, so a flush while the seal stands does not take what the guest stored before it.

Keep across a seal the digests of a page unjournaled at it, so a capture under the seal leaves out a block the guest put back to the journal's old bytes, which the selected checkpoint no longer holds.
Keep the digests of a capture whose journal write failed, so the next capture leaves out the blocks the failed entry held.
Answer a durable flush whose journal sync failed as a success, so the guest believes blocks durable that may not be on the disk.
Leave the pages of a capture whose journal write failed captured, so the next flush does not take them again.
Read a checkpoint's covered position at its selection rather than its pause, so it covers captures made after the guest ran again and a replay never applies them.
Let a VM holding more than half the journal's ring commit more without waiting for its own checkpoint.
Keep running a VM whose journal a reader at a newer epoch has read, so two instances of the guest run.
Stop counting a detaching memory region as attached before its layer's pages are back, so a pager closed meanwhile releases its files under the pages the detach then frees into them.
Evict a page a guest maps when a cancelled prefetch gave its slots back between the allocation's look for a free slot and its eviction step, rather than take one of those slots.
Evict a page a guest maps for a fault's slot while a prefetch holds free slots for pages nobody has asked for yet, rather than cancel that prefetch.
Prefetch the rest of every fault's run, whether or not the fault follows a recent fault of its memory region. A chain of faults at random then prefetches on every hop.

Read a fault at random's page alone even in a pager that prefetches at random, as every pager did from 2026-10-04 until the real application's restore. A guest of 2 MiB pages touching its heap at random then faults once a page instead of once a run.

Plan the window of a fault that prefetches before its own page's read starts, as every fault did. Each hop of a chain of 4 KiB faults reading forwards then pays the window's planning on top of its read.

Plan the whole window of a fault at random, every page of it located and looked up among the resident pages, as every fault did, rather than its page alone. Each hop of a chain of 4 KiB faults at random then pays the window's planning on top of its read, and maps the window's resident pages it will not read.
Fetch and decode a segment's page table for every lookup instead of taking the table the page cache keeps. Every index then decodes the segment again for every page it locates.
Lose loaded or copied data when creating a resident page.
Locate every member at the start of its part.
Reclaim the checkpoints the selected one still reads from.
Reclaim a kept checkpoint no fork was taken from, as if only pins protected anything.
Compact a parent's checkpoint into its child, which bills the child for the parent's page.
Accept a Starter's snapshot load request that names a key this package loads. Linux only, as root.
Leave the prepared directory and its sockets to this process instead of the placement's Owner. Linux only, as root.
Give the VMM host paths instead of the placement's Within. Linux only, as root.
Let a Starter prepare one launch twice. Linux only, as root.
Admit a memory session from a process other than the VMM its Starter reported. Linux only, as root.
Restore an x86_64 guest without asking the VMM to move its clock on by the time its state spent stopped.
Accept a guest kernel without the VMGenID driver, or boot arguments that hide the device from it.
Count a sparse spill file at what it holds rather than at its promise.
Take the filesystem's size as the host's room, ignoring what other writers hold.
Tell a cache over its share to stop at its share rather than one region below it.
Admit a cache write the write budget cannot afford.
Keep the write budget's reserves for the lowest priorities instead of the highest.
Count spill promises at what they hold when the promises do not fit, so the host reports ready.
Let the cache fill the disk to the floor, leaving another host on the filesystem no room to promise a VM's staging.
Judge whether promises fit the filesystem by the space other writers leave now, so a host waiting for them is refused.
Serve a page cache disk item that names another key.
Serve a page cache disk item without checking its checksum.
Write every read item of an evicted disk region again, past half a region.
Let fills take the disk region kept free for the second chance.
Give an evicted disk region back while a read is still in flight from it.
Write a closed disk region's table before its items are synced.
Have a closed pull free what it copied, as pulls held regions before.
Index the region that was open when the host stopped, which has no table, instead of giving it back.
Keep a page cache disk file that names another deployment, whose page identities may name other bytes.
Give back a disk region whose table is torn without scanning its items.
Write the membership without the condition on the object read, so a writer that lost the race writes over another's change and the generation goes back.
Admit assigning a disk to another member while its member still holds it, before it is released and let go.
Answer a cache request under whatever generation the host holds: neither read a newer one first nor tell the sender it is stale.
Serve the disk a request names whether or not the membership at its generation has this host serve it.
Take a holder's answer that the sender is stale as a miss, instead of reading the membership and asking again.
Weigh the host's disk by the disk limiter's moving share instead of the disk it is given.
Refuse to start a host whose promises fit the filesystem but not the space another writer holds now.
Open the page cache's file without its lock, so two hosts on one node share one file.
Accept a cache directory on another filesystem than the scratch, which the one disk limiter does not measure.
Close a pulled VM's pull when its machine ends, so the checkpoint a stop publishes after that keeps nothing on the disk.
Take the code from the number of disks wanted now, so a drain changes it and every stripe becomes a miss.
Forget the member of a host pod that did not answer one survey, so the membership drains it.
Rebuild an envelope from stripes of another code whose length fits this one.
Give up when the first k stripes fail the envelope's check, instead of rebuilding from other sets of k to find the wrong one.
Look a stripe up in the disk's index under any code, so a page kept under another code is read and refused instead of missed.
Read the disk under the list's code alone, so a page kept under the code the deployment used before is a miss.
Read the cluster under the list's code alone, so a deliberate change of the code sends every earlier window to the store.
Leave a window read under an earlier code under it, so it is never filled under the deployment's code and every read of it asks the new code's ranks first for nothing.
Find a page's first item in the disk's index whatever index was asked for, as an index that holds one stripe a page.
Put stripe i on rank i alone, dropping the indices a list shorter than the code is wide has no rank for.
Keep a stripe the rebuild of its envelope found wrong, so it is read again until its region goes.
Place every window by the list of caches, ignoring the share the cluster cache is turned on for, so a host with others in its list keeps a pulled VM as stripes it cannot rebuild alone.
Mark a peer down when a dial failed because its own caller gave up.
Close the connection of a request over its peer's budget instead of answering BUSY on it.
Count every class of a peer's requests against one budget, so a stream at its budget makes faults busy.
Send each reply as soon as it is built rather than after the replies to the requests before it.
Give up on a peer that closes a hello unanswered instead of speaking version 1 to it.
Never close a connection that hears nothing, so a request over a partition waits until it heals.
Send bulk reads without the host's background budget, so a fault's reply waits behind all the stream's bytes.
Let requests woken from a wait for room go on to the wire without being admitted again, so the Go scheduler orders the requests one dial or release wakes together.
Answer a cache request that names another cache, as a reused address would.
Queue a keep over the background budget instead of dropping it.
Send stripe reads without the bound on stripe bytes in flight.
Close a connection over a hello a duplicating link delivered twice, racing the dialer's first request.
Send stripe reads over the fault class, where a stripe waits behind every 2 MiB page reply ahead of it on its connection.
Run a pull's reads in a slot of the loads faults wait on, so a fault waits behind a pull's read of the store.
Read every page a pull reaches from the store, as before a pull asked the cluster what it holds.
Count a page held when any rank holds any stripe of it, so a page with fewer than k stripes is never pulled.
Have a pull's read of a segment through the cluster read the store as well past its bound, as a fault's does.
Leave a pull's reads unmarked, so they ask second requests, teach the delay and go over the fault and stripe classes.
Send a prefetch's stripe requests over the stripe class faults use, since they run under the reads' life rather than the read's context.
Count the ranks that answer a presence check stale as holding nothing, rather than read the newer membership and ask again.
Leave a pull reading while the host is short of memory or disk.
Send every presence check over the fault class, so a pull's checks share the connections a guest's faults wait on.
Serve stripes past the host's serving bandwidth instead of answering BUSY.
Hand back a raw page as a slice of its reply's pooled buffer, which the next reply is read into.
End a request's receive context before its payload is read, so a socket's read deadline fails every keep.
Fill the cluster with a part before its PUT has succeeded.
Take a keep for a window the cache's own list does not rank it for.
Fill in front of a read of the store: its callers wait for the right, the split and the keeps.
Fill from every read of the store, with no fill right asked of rank 1.
Drop a publication's fill when the queue is full, as a read's is, rather than wait for room.
Let a publication's fills wait for room, the rate, the budget or a busy holder without a bound.
Take a publication's fills before a read's, on the worker of fills and on each holder's lane, so a read's fill waits behind them.
Queue a keep for stripes the cache is already writing rather than drop it.
Ask fill rights on goroutines of their own, and send each keep a lane holds beside the one before it, so the scheduler orders them on the holder's link.
Take from each rank only the indices the list puts on it, which a change of ranks leaves few of (B5).
Ask every one of a window's first k+m ranks at once rather than k+1.
Ask a window's ranks in rank order, so every reader asks the same k+1 and the rest are never asked.
Never ask the rest of a window's ranks after the delay, so a read waits for its slowest holder.
Ask the rest of a window's ranks after the delay whatever the budget holds.
Leave a stripe a rebuild found wrong with its holder rather than telling it to drop it.
Read the store past the bound whatever the token bucket holds.
Count a holder that holds nothing of a window as one that timed out.
Mark down every host that times out, past a fifth of the list.
Probe a host marked down every second rather than after ten seconds growing to sixty.
Send fills to a host the reads have marked down.
Repair a rank with the index the list puts on it, whether or not another rank holds it.
Never check, by a HEAD, that the part behind a sampled hit still exists.
Keep one delay and one store bound for reads of every size, so a large read after many small fast ones reads the store too.
Keep a page rebuilt under k = 1 as a view of its peer's reply buffer, which the next reply is read into.
Leave a read's requests out of what settling the reads waits for, so the requests of a read the store answered first still run after it, into the next batch of reads.
Hand each part of a publication to the fills as its PUT ends, so the scheduler orders a host's fills.
Decide a fill's next holder only once the last one's keep is answered, so a host sends one keep at a time and a publication goes at a holder's pace times its holders.
Decide the holders of a later publication's fill while an earlier one waits for room on a holder's lane, so a holder receives a later window's keep before an earlier one's.
Queue a publication's window as a view of its part, so the queue counts the window and the host holds the whole part.
Write a publication's part to the hot tier before its regional PUT has succeeded.
Fail a read whose hot tier failed rather than read the regional bucket.
Give a store a hot tier beside a cache that fills the cluster.
Copy a missed object, or write a published one, to the hot tier in front of the read or the publication.
Hold every fill of the hot tier, whatever the queue's bound.
Drop the remembered survey only when a move begins, so a survey a host's read of the list of caches took during a start answers the command sent after it.
Report a fork's root as soon as its root publication installs, before it gives back its hold on the point it was forked at.
Ignore a shard's lease: open a shard under an assignment older than the one its header names, and keep writing one whose lease another member took.
Answer a journal batch's commits once its write returns, before its sync. A commit is answered while its sync is held, and one whose sync a power loss interrupted is answered and then lost.
Run no commit's Full hook, so a commit the commits placed ahead of it left no room for waits for trims nobody asks for.
Pad over a failed batch's range only in a batch with a commit, so a commit that does not fit beside the range waits for a trim that frees nothing.
Serve a journal read without fencing its VM at the reader's epoch, so a commit at the older epoch is still placed and answered after the read.
Let a releasing shard go while the cloud still has it attached to a machine, or cannot say where it is.
Let a host's own releasing disk go only once its host is gone, so a pod replaced over the disk while its member drained never serves it again.
Let a host's own releasing disk go on a copy that read the release of an earlier assignment of the disk, after which the host may have served it again.
Detach a releasing shard from its machine while its host still holds it open.
Open a shard by the membership the host holds, without reading the object again first, so a host behind takes a shard that moved to another host on its machine.
Take a terminating host pod for one that stays, so its shards stay on it until its node is gone.
Encode a publication's pages one batch at a time, so it runs at one encoder's pace however many the store has.
Wait for each part's PUT before filling the next, so a publication has one part in flight however many upload slots the store has.
Have each batch's goroutine take its own encoder, so the Go scheduler, not the order the batches were filled, decides which batch is encoded first.
Arm no bound on an object store request, so a GET whose headers never come waits as long as the store holds it, as one GET of Cloud Storage waited 52 minutes.
Read a stalled body on from another object than the one it began as, so its caller holds bytes of two objects.
Time a cache's reads of the cluster by the wall clock when it has no table of peers, ignoring the clock it was given.
Take a reply that arrived after the backing was closed, before the goroutine that ends the request in flight ran.
Take the parent's answer to a fork child's claim once the receive was closed, so a child its host gave up is reported claimed.
Take the source's listing of what it holds once the backing was closed.

Make an AwaitingClean page Dirty in place on a store, as Zircon does, against D1. The checkpoint then reads the bytes stored after its pause, and the store gets no copy. Each test fails alone: one stores through a lookup, the other through the pager's DirtyPages.
Leave the pages of an abandoned writeback AwaitingClean, as Zircon has no abandon, against D4. The failed checkpoint keeps its pages and the copies it held, and the mappings it protected stay.
Attach a journal disk reserved for a machine only once its member is assigned it, so a new host waits a whole attach before it serves durable flush.
Make no journal disk for a machine of the pool that has none, so its host never serves durable flush.
Let a step mark deleting a journal disk that is not released and empty, so flushed writes not yet in a checkpoint are deleted with it.
Open a journal disk assigned to this host as a cache shard, which empties it of its flushed writes.
Close a VM whose replay failed part way with its final checkpoint, which publishes part of the journals' entries and drops the journals that hold the rest.
Resume a VM from its checkpoint's VMM state after its open replayed flushed writes into its disks, so registers from before those writes run over the disks after them.
Journal and answer a flush before the VM's record names this host's journal at its epoch, so a recovery never replays it.
Drop the source's journal from the record at a checkpoint paused before the post-copy ended, which may not hold every page the source held.
Read again a page of the window that a prefetch has landed but not yet given up, so the prefetch's copy is dropped as a duplicate.
Plan a fault that waited for a prefetch again as soon as the prefetch's supply wakes it, while the prefetch still holds the run, so the fault maps its own page alone.

Look for the reads under way before taking the host's lock to send a prefetch's requests, so another fork's prefetch of the same root sent in between is unseen and the requests meet: the pager panics.
Serve a journal read the VM's entries of every epoch after the covered position, so a VM back on a host it ran on replays its entries of the earlier stay over a newer checkpoint.
Answer a flush on a migration's destination before its post-copy ends, though the pages the guest stored into on the source are in no journal yet.
Hold an open back as pending while its record names a journal disk let go holding nothing, so a VM whose host died after a checkpoint covered its flushes never opens again.
Answer a durable flush of a VMM the host started and has not registered yet, with nothing journaled, as a destination's guest sends the flushes it held again as soon as it runs.
Add a journal disk a listing names over a generation newer than the listing's, which may add back a disk another controller deleted and removed.
Mark a journal disk empty on a report under an assignment older than the disk's, so a host that read it for a lost host marks the disk it now writes.
Report the journal disk a host writes empty before the membership releases it, so a VM placed late flushes to a disk that may be deleted.
Take a VM on a host whose own journal disk the membership releases, so its flushes go to a disk about to be reported empty.

Let an eviction of a region's own page go on without holding the region live, so a detach gives its reservations back and destroys its layer under it: the eviction reads a freed slot and writes into a reservation no longer the region's.
Panic when a fault waits on a prefetch request the prefetch's supply already answered, rather than answer the request it sends at once.
Look at whether a published page's owner maps it before its detach is kept out, so a detach in between leaves the page to be supplied to a destroyed layer: the pager panics.
Survey a run read's window by the names located before its region was given up, so a page a retire named anew joins by its parent's name.
Give the region up for a run's read while the plan holds the region's own page, which a retire waits for with the region held.

Map a refaulted page by the protection read before the region was given up for its slot. A capture taken meanwhile that journaled and protected the page leaves it mapped writable and not unjournaled, so the guest's next store reaches no flush.

Give up the idle page allocateOwn chose under h.mu once its lock is taken, without asking again whether it is idle. A page a settle handed back to the region meanwhile, and an eviction's look aged, is freed while the region names it: the pager panics.

Let a settle's reshare, which holds the region exclusively, wait for the lock of the root's page a copy was made from. A prefetch holding that page waits for a window's stripe, a fault holding the stripe waits for the region, and nothing moves.

Let a capture, which holds the region exclusively, wait for the lock of the page a dirty page was copied from. A fault holding that root's page in its plan waits to take the region back after its read, and the two wait for each other.

Let a lookup of a page that is the region's own state go on past its layer, to a root's page or the volume, once an eviction spilled the page after the fault looked at it. The guest reads bytes it had stored over: its store is lost.

Take a lent root's copies before its lent pages, trusting the seal's end to have taken every lent page out under its lock. A retire that published a page under another name left its lent page, a child's copy of it made meanwhile stays in the root, and the point's file is dropped while the child maps the copy.

Count a page in one of a page's own places that nothing maps and no root holds, which an eviction is taking, as one the region maps. A refault meeting it beside the checkpoint's copy reports both places taken, and the guest's session ends with ErrCapacity.
Leave the cold copies a seal found unchanged out of both its set and the region's dirty set when a later compare fails. A store into one is then dirty in no set, and no checkpoint holds it.

Keep a fork point's lent name for a page until the point's fork ends rather than take it away as the page leaves the checkpoint, so a child faulting in between maps a freed slot or reads the parent's later stores.
Destroy an unpublished lent root at its seal's end, with the pages a child read under the point's name and still maps: the pager panics.
Let a share lend a checkpoint's pages after its seal ended, registering a lent root and a lent entry nothing ever ends.
Free a fork file's number in its holder before the holder's DROP_FILE lands, so another point's file is given under the number about to be dropped.
Give a page back from an abandoned seal without the protection a capture gave it, so a read fault maps it writable while it is not unjournaled and the guest's next store reaches no flush.

Read a spilled page of a checkpoint without holding the region live, so a detach between the look at its reservation and the read frees the reservation, and the read fails or reads another page's bytes.

Let a lookup go down into the root its resolver named without asking under the root's lock whether it still holds the page, so a READ goes to a root's source without h.mu, where a prefetch's send meets it and panics, or to a lent root its seal's end removed.

Let a rule copy a page of another read-ahead window without its stripe, and wait for that page's lock. A store of the page in between makes it private twice and the run maps a punched slot; a fault holding the page across its read, behind a queued seal, deadlocks with the store.
Join an already-private page to a store's run without holding it, so an eviction before the command frees the slot the command maps.
Keep waiting for a private page's own offset after another range took a shared arena's last extent, evicting until that range loses its page.
Make a range whole around a refused store whose page copied away from a sealed one to another offset, mapping the guest's page onto the checkpoint's copy.
Copy a page a store read into the region's own file as though it were a root's. The copy's supply loses and the region maps a punched slot.
Number a Buggify site's calls across every task in arrival order even in a controlled run, so two tasks that run at one instant shift each other's firings and a seed no longer replays.

Give up the recovery after a lost source when the source still serves the pages, although its hold is over by the orchestrator's clock and its own timer lets them go a moment later: the VM is left stopped.
Let a survey take up a handover this orchestrator is still carrying, between a failed carry and its recovery, so two recoveries of one VM race and one fails finding the other's open.

Write-protect the runs a capture read as it took its pages, before it held the region's protection, so a page an eviction unmapped in between is protected unmapped: the client refuses and the region is terminal.

Count a store's lost read of the page it copies as one of a fault's eight decisions whether it needs a page of its own, so a store that loses it eight times running to other forks reading the same page ends its guest's session with ErrContended.

Look at a prefetch's request after the source let it go, so a supply of its pages by another region's fault that completes it in between makes the prefetch panic that it met another read, or fail the provider's assertion.

Let go of the page a store's copy replaces before the store's command lands, so the end of a fork point's seal drops the copy the guest still maps, which has no alias left to revoke: its slot is given back and its file dropped under the guest's mapping.

Move a page to the harvested queue without taking its mappings away, so the guest reads on through them without a fault, nothing marks the page accessed, and the evictor takes a page the guest keeps reading.

Record a run mapped although the client refused its command, so a dirty page is recorded mapped with nothing installed, and the guest's next store into it resolves writable over nothing: UFFDIO_CONTINUE on the client's anonymous trap, invalid argument.
Fail an attach whose population a client refused for want of mapping budget, so a fork whose inherited pages a 4 KiB client cannot map at once does not start, although population only saves faults.

Take a failed capture's protected mappings away still holding the region's protection, which the revocation takes shared: the capture waits for itself with the region held, the guest's flush never ends and its machine never detaches.

Leave a store's old read-only mapping in place when the client refuses the writable one, the binding already the region's own writable page, so the next fault resolves writable over a read-only mapping.
